Balmora: extended vs 2.0

2D layouts from Magna Urbis (unmodified, rev 21e2217) via scrib-worldgen settle, 2026-11-24. Same population (3000) and seed in every map. Click a map to open it full size.

What to look at

  • Which arm reads more like a town you want to walk through: the old core grown outward (A) or a new town astride the gorge (B).
  • Street tissue per style: organic lanes (european-organic), dense alleys and dead ends (medina), a grid (korean). These are Magna Urbis's own styles as stand-ins; Morrowind styles (Hlaalu, Redoran, Telvanni) come later as data.
  • How the new streets meet the river: bridges, quays, which bank holds the centre.
  • Rate by elimination: reject / maybe / keep, per map.

Known limits

  • Flattened relief in both arms. Vanilla Balmora's hills (slope ~0.35-0.49) and the 10x Odai gorge (banks 23-25 m, slope ~0.21) are steeper than Magna Urbis lets a street climb (0.12), so both plan on 1/4 relief. In game, the terrain under the new quarters gets regraded to match (the standard step under generated towns).
  • Arm A drops swamp pools under 2500 m². Arm B gets one straight founding road across the narrowest water near the centre, as a region generator would give it.
  • Lots and streets only: no buildings yet. In game, Morrowind's own buildings go on these lots.

A. Old Balmora extended

Vanilla Balmora kept as is (dark), new town grown around it, joining its 5 road exits. Vanilla terrain, planned at 1/4 relief.

B. Balmora 2.0

No old part. New town on both banks of the 10x world's Odai gorge, with a founding road crossing. Planned at 1/4 relief.
